title: A resumed worker reset a shared job cache and erased the records it needed to harvest a teammate’s jobs

source.evidence_note: Observed local historical transcript; see evidence/incident.md. Source aliases map privately; Submission of these prepared files was authorized on 2026-10-11.

horizon.intervening_work: The worker had paused for about eleven hours; a fork advanced the same lane during that interval. On resume, the coordinator explicitly described the new jobs. Git stash/rebase synchronization was attempted before harvesting.
horizon.mechanism: Observed destructive cleanup of shared runtime state at a resume boundary. The explicit handoff named the teammate jobs immediately before the reset, so this also has a short-distance explanation; long-context causation is untested.

failure.expected_behavior: Resume a lane, harvest the replication jobs already submitted by a fork, and confirm the result before broader evaluation.
failure.observed_behavior: After receiving explicit fork-job identifiers, the resumed worker restored a tracked shared runtime cache from HEAD during Git synchronization. The cache then lacked the job identifiers; polling required the erased identifier-to-cluster mapping, so a completed evaluation was not harvested.

comparison_note: No model attempt or causal control has run. A scripted faulty fixture and correct reference, where recorded, validate the checker only.
